accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Year 3 Forces and magnets statutory requirement (notice that some forces need contact between two objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance) and the Year 5 gravity statement. Contact examples (push, pull by hand, friction) and non-contact examples (magnetism, gravity) are correct; magnetism acting through thin paper and card is correct; the pull falling with distance is described as fading, not switching off. The 0–5 cm pull values (10, 7, 4.5, 2.5, 1.2, 0.5) and the 3 cm jump gap are labelled in the adult text as a model.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: magnets must touch to pull; a magnet's pull stops at a fixed distance rather than weakening; friction called non-contact because it is invisible; any material blocks magnetism; a floating ring magnet rests on nothing; and objects moving 'on their own' with no force. Each appears as a prediction option or challenge distractor with its own feedback.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaggapforce is built around the gap between two objects: a hand that only moves the ball at 0 cm, a magnet slid in 1 cm steps until a clip jumps at 3 cm, a force-against-gap chart comparing hand and magnet, a barrier test with paper, card and a thick book, a contact/non-contact sort and a floating ring magnet. flagmag (what a magnet attracts), flagpoles (which poles attract) and flagfvoc (force words) have no gap measurement. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the hand fail to move the ball from a gap before reading the word contact; watches the purple pull arrow grow as the gap shrinks and the clip jump at 3 cm; builds a chart where the hand bar is zero at every gap above 0 while the magnet bars fall gradually; sees paper and card hold the clip while the book drops it; and pushes the floating ring down to feel it spring back.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with a tempting wrong option each: 'yes, if you push hard enough' (contact from a gap), 'no, magnets must touch to pull', 'stops as soon as there is a gap', 'no, the card blocks it', 'non-contact, because you cannot see it' (friction) and 'nothing: it floats on air'. The lab result disproves each one.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions; wrong answers are tagged touch, far, nothing, strong, same, grav or fric, and each tag names the slip: no touching so not contact, the foot and ball are pressed together, things do not start moving by themselves, magnets pull hardest close up, the pull changes with the gap (10 at 0 cm to 2.5 at 3 cm), gravity pulls down not back, friction needs rubbing surfaces.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.3 (family target ≤ 5): short sentences, contact and non-contact each defined from a concrete example (kicking a ball, magnet and clip). Adult text grade 6.0 (target ≤ 10) after splitting the mistakes list into separate sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any lesson. Kid paragraphs: contact forces, non-contact forces, the gap, gravity and thin barriers. Adult paragraphs: curriculum placement, physics and model caveat, five named mistakes, what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in both themes: after the first pass the touch step's gap label was fixed to say the ball rolled away instead of showing a growing gap, and the magnet ruler was redrawn to run from the clip (0) back to 5 cm so it no longer ran off the right edge. Chart labels, sort boxes and ring magnets fit the 390 px canvas; buttons wrap to two rows.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Push with a gap / Push touching, 1 cm closer / back (labelled 'Move the magnet 1 cm closer/back') / Start again, Magnet / Hand with aria-pressed, Gap − / Gap + / Measure, paper / card / thick book with aria-pressed, Contact / Non-contact, Flip the top ring / Push it down. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the gap, force value or result. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
